items.area: Online video OPD run for Uttar Pradesh; used from home in Mathura (no clinic visit)

fee.basis: eSanjeevani FAQ 1: "No, you don't have to pay anything to anybody for using National Telemedicine Service."

items.area: National phone helpline, callable from Mathura (no clinic visit)
items.access_conditions: Open to anyone with a mental health concern, their family members, and ASHAs or community volunteers calling for someone (FAQ 5). It is not an emergency service: the FAQ says emergencies such as suicide risk need doctors at a hospital.
items.notes: The site lists 14416 and 1-800 891 4416 as toll-free numbers. It does not state whether counselling or consultation has a fee, so MedAssist shows Fee not listed. FAQ 10 says video consultations with e-prescriptions are now offered.
